pageCache.text:
Welcome To The Write Time School
Everyone achieves. Everyone succeeds.
The Write Time is an independent SEN school for students in Key Stages 3 to Post-16, providing personalised education, mentoring and therapeutic support that helps every young person thrive.Proud to be the UK’s first William Glasser Quality School.
It’s Not Until They Know That You Care, They Will Care About What You Know.
Thinking about The Write Time for your child? We’re here to help.
We support young people in Key Stages 3 to Post-16 with Special Educational Needs who benefit from a highly personalised learning environment, therapeutic support and mentoring.
Our unique approach
At The Write Time we use Choice Theory to empower students to take control of their learning and personal growth. Each student follows a personalised learning pathway, supported by mentoring and therapeutic programmes. Our small class sizes are led by a qualified teacher and a Learning Development Tutor, ensuring that every learner receives the focused, individual attention they need.
Education & School Life
At The Write Time, we offer a broad curriculum tailored to meet the unique needs of each student.
Tailored Learning PlansEvery student benefits from a bespoke educational plan, ensuring both academic and personal growth.
Bespoke CurriculumDesigned to meet individual needs, fostering personal & academic growth and life skills.
QualificationsWhether aiming for further education or entering the workforce, we provide the skills and qualifications students need.
Therapeutic SupportOur comprehensive range of therapies supports students, helping them thrive.
Sports & Recreation A focus on social skills, confidence, and independence through engaging activities.
Progress UpdatesTransparent, termly progress reports for parents, carers, and local authorities.
success stories
Headteacher’s welcome
Hear from our Headteacher, Lana Philipson, as she shares what makes The Write Time different and how our personalised approach helps every student feel valued, supported and able to succeed.
It is a privilege to welcome you to The Write Time Independent School. We believe that every young person deserves a safe and inspiring space to learn, grow, and reach their full potential. At The Write Time, our team is dedicated to supporting every child academically, personally, and emotionally, so they can thrive both in school and in life.
As the first Glasser School in the UK, we pride ourselves on supporting our pupils using Choice Theory and Reality Therapy as the keys to unlock their potential and achieve their very best. At The Write Time, our dedicated and experienced staff ensure that every pupil follows a bespoke curriculum, one that marries specialist support to an appropriate curriculum that has been purposefully planned to achieve individual goals in academic, vocational and personal development – staff teams focus on EHC targets and ensure that every pupil has access to therapeutic input that meets individual special needs.
Our curriculum is tailored to each student’s needs, incorporating specialist SEN support, vocational opportunities, and a wide range of qualifications including GCSEs, Functional Skills, and vocational awards.
Our spacious and safe school site enriches our curriculum offer, providing airy learning spaces that enable pupils to fully engage in learning that is experiential, progressive and fully supported by our therapeutic curriculum. The school layout encourages our pupils to feel nurtured, accepted and empowered to take on new challenges throughout their learning journey and be prepared to take their next steps as well-rounded citizens, ready to integrate into society.We’d love to welcome you to The Write Time. To arrange a visit and experience our school first-hand, please contact our school office.
Empowering Every Student to Succeed
We believe our students deserve to engage in a curriculum including academic, personal & social, and vocational learning. This is why, as an independent secondary school, we work with students with a variety of additional needs, including (but not limited to): ASD, Asperger’s, ADHD, Global Developmental Delay, PTSD, Dyslexia, and Dyscalculia.
every student receives the personalised support they need to Thrive
We combine specialised SEN support with tailored curricula and specialist support, which allows our students to thrive in a nurturing environment. Our goal is to equip young people with the skills and confidence they need for a bright future.
Approved for up to 90 students
KS3 to Post-16 provision
Specialist Therapeutic Support
Ofsted material change successfully approved
Get in touch
Have questions or want to learn more about how we can support your child? Get in touch with us today.
info@thewritetime.org.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: About The Write Time | Independent SEN School
pageCache.text:
About The Write Time
A nurturing independent SEN school where every young person is supported to achieve, grow in confidence and prepare for a successful future.
Everyone achieves. Everyone succeeds.
At The Write Time, every young person is valued, understood and supported to achieve their full potential. As an independent SEN school for students in Key Stages 3 to Post-16, we combine personalised education, mentoring and specialist therapeutic support to help every learner build confidence, develop independence and prepare for a successful future.Following a successful Ofsted Material Change, we are now approved to support up to 90 students and have expanded our provision to include Post-16 pathways in Food Technology, Arts Award and IT. Working closely with families, we create personalised learning journeys that enable every student to thrive academically, socially and emotionally.
William Glasser Quality School
Leaders in Safeguarding Accreditation
Matrix Accreditation – View the Matrix report
Why Families Choose The Write Time
Every young person deserves an education that recognises their individual strengths, nurtures their confidence and prepares them for life beyond school. At The Write Time, our personalised approach combines specialist support, meaningful relationships and high expectations to help every student achieve their full potential.
Personalised Learning
Every student follows an individual learning pathway tailored to their strengths, interests and aspirations. Small class sizes and bespoke programmes ensure each young person receives the support and challenge they need to succeed.
Specialist Support
Our education is enhanced by mentoring and specialist therapeutic support, helping students build confidence, develop emotional wellbeing and overcome barriers to learning in a safe and nurturing environment.
Preparation for Life
We prepare students for successful futures through academic and vocational qualifications, independent living skills, employability opportunities and Post-16 pathways that build confidence for adulthood.
Take a Look Around The Write Time
Watch our short school walkthrough to explore our learning environment and see The Write Time in action.
Our story
The Write Time was founded on a simple belief: every young person deserves the opportunity to succeed in an environment where they feel understood, supported and valued.
As an independent SEN school for students in Key Stages 3 to Post-16, we provide a highly personalised education that recognises every student’s individual strengths, interests and aspirations. By combining tailored learning, specialist support and meaningful relationships, we help young people build confidence, achieve recognised qualifications and develop the skills they need for life beyond school.
Following a successful Ofsted Material Change, The Write Time is now approved to support up to 90 students and has expanded its provision to include Post-16 pathways in Food Technology, Arts Award and IT. We continue to grow while remaining committed to the values that have always shaped our school: high expectations, strong relationships and a genuine belief in every student’s potential.
Young People SupportedSince opening in 2014, we’ve helped more than 500 young people develop the confidence, skills and qualifications needed for further education, employment and independent living.
“Students like coming to school because they feel supported. They say staff are fun, friendly and kind.”
Choice Theory in Practice
Our educational philosophy is rooted in William Glasser’s Choice Theory, encouraging students to take responsibility, build positive relationships and recognise the choices they have to shape their own future.
“My favourite thing about being at The Write Time is I feel like I am in one big happy family, and I enjoy all of my lessons. However, I really enjoy my mentoring sessions with Eddy.”
Meet the People Behind The Write Time
Every member of our team shares a commitment to building trusting relationships, recognising individual strengths and helping every student achieve success in their own way.
Chris Murray
Chris founded The Write Time in 2014, combining academic learning with personal development and mentoring to build students’ confidence and self-belief, helping them explore new opportunities.
Lana Philippson
Headteacher, DDSL & SENCO
Lana has over 20 years of experience working with young people with Special Educational Needs. She has served as Deputy Head and an English and Humanities teacher at The Write Time.
Emma Dear
DEputy headteacher & DSL
Emma has over 10 years experience working with young people with Special Educational Needs in a range of settings. She is also our Humanities Teacher at The Write Time.
Debbie brindle-Carter
ASSISTANT headteacher
Debbie has over 14 years experience with SEN, in a professional capacity as well as a mother of an SEN child. Debbie has been at The Write Time for over 2 years and has served as PSHE and Food Tech Teacher.
Lou Coleman
Relational Integrative Therapist
Lou is an experienced Feldenkrais Practitioner, movement specialist, and qualified psychotherapist. She has many years of experience supporting students in learning through movement, using sensory integration, a respectful hands-on approach, deep pressure, and body-based approaches to reduce anxiety.
Josh Considine
Josh has over 10 years’ experience supporting young people with Special Educational Needs. He is passionate about the value of creativity and its positive impact on mental health and emotional wellbeing, using music to help people express emotions, improve communication, build confidence, reduce anxiety, and strengthen social connections.
Jasmine Murray
Junior Operations Manager
Jasmine has over 5 years of experience working with young people in a variety of settings; Youth Clubs, Primary Schools, Sports Camps, University, and previously being a Learning Development Tutor (LDT) within the school. Jasmine will be supporting with marketing, health and safety, finance, and mentoring the students at TWT.
Amanda Murray
Amanda works tirelessly in her spare time to ensure that The Write Time meets its statutory obligations as well as giving financial and strategic advice. She works for a top FTSE company as a Senior Group Accountant and we are fortunate to have access to her expertise.
Moira Oliver
Moira is a qualified tutor, trainer, and counsellor in Choice Theory, with a passion for supporting TWT in gaining ‘Glasser Quality School’ status. She’s been involved with Choice Theory since 2005.
Paul Keenleyside
Paul is a leadership consultant and former headteacher with 15 years of classroom experience. He specialises in leadership coaching and has held senior roles in both education and the third sector.
Trusted by Local Authorities
Partnering with local authorities and vocational organisations to deliver a holistic education.
Accredited by
Recognised by leading organisations for our commitment to high-quality education, safeguarding and continuous improvement.
View our latest Ofsted report.
Come and See The Write Time
We’d love to welcome you to The Write Time. Arrange a visit to meet our team, explore the school and discover how we support every student to achieve their potential.

Specialist Support
Helping every young person feel understood, supported and ready to thrive.
Every student is unique, which is why support at The Write Time is never one-size-fits-all. Our personalised approach combines mentoring, specialist therapies and close partnership with families to help every young person overcome barriers to learning, develop confidence and achieve their potential.
Support Built Around Every Student
We begin by understanding each young person’s strengths, interests and individual needs. Working closely with families and professionals, we create personalised support that develops alongside every student throughout their journey with us.
PersonalisedSupport tailored to every learner.
CollaborativeWorking closely with families and professionals.
HolisticSupporting emotional, social and academic development.
Support Journey
Every student follows a personalised journey of support. Working together, our mentors, therapists, teachers and families create a consistent approach that helps every young person feel understood, build confidence and make meaningful progress both in and beyond the classroom.
Personalised Mentoring
Every student is assigned a dedicated mentor who builds trusted relationships, encourages positive choices and provides consistent guidance throughout their time at The Write Time.

Specialist Therapies
Every student’s therapeutic programme is designed around their individual needs and may include specialist support from experienced practitioners.
Speech & Language Therapy
Helping students develop communication, confidence and social interaction.
Supporting emotional expression, self-awareness and wellbeing through creativity.
Providing a safe and creative way to express emotions, build confidence and strengthen communication.
Feldenkrais Movement
Supports body awareness, coordination and emotional regulation through gentle movement and sensory learning.
Why Therapy Matters
Therapeutic support isn’t separate from learning. By helping students regulate emotions, build confidence and strengthen communication, therapy removes barriers that allow young people to engage more fully in education and everyday life.
Speech & Language Therapy
Building Confidence Through Communication
Communication underpins every aspect of learning, relationships and independence. Our Speech and Language Therapy supports students to develop the skills they need to express themselves confidently, understand others and participate more fully in school life.

Expressing Feelings Through Creativity
Art Therapy provides a safe and supportive environment where students can explore thoughts and emotions that may be difficult to express through words. Creative activities encourage self-expression while helping students develop emotional resilience, confidence and self-awareness.

Every session is tailored to the individual, helping students develop greater understanding of themselves while supporting their overall wellbeing.

Music Therapy offers students a creative and engaging way to express themselves, communicate and build meaningful relationships. Through singing, instruments, music technology and improvisation, students develop confidence, emotional regulation and communication skills in a safe therapeutic environment.
Music Therapy supports:
For many students, music provides another language through which they can connect with themselves and others.

Learning Through Movement
Feldenkrais Movement helps students develop body awareness, coordination and emotional regulation through gentle movement and sensory learning. By strengthening the connection between the brain and body, students build the confidence, independence and practical skills needed for everyday life.
Sessions may support:
Learning through movement enables students to feel more comfortable, capable and engaged in both school and everyday activities.

Every Child Receives Different Support
No two students require exactly the same support. Some may benefit from mentoring, while others access one or more specialist therapies alongside their education. Every programme is tailored to the individual needs, strengths and aspirations of the young person.
Working in Partnership With Families
We believe the best outcomes happen when school and home work together. Parents and carers are an important part of every student’s journey, and we are committed to building open, supportive relationships throughout their time at The Write Time.
Families are involved through:
By working together, we ensure every young person receives consistent support both at school and at home.
Specialist Support in Action

– Ed, Support Worker

Meet Our Specialists
Behind every student’s success is a dedicated team of experienced professionals. Our therapists and specialist staff work closely together to provide personalised support that helps each young person overcome barriers, build confidence and thrive.
Ashna
Speech and Language Therapist
Ashna has over 18 years’ experience working across NHS and independent settings, supporting children and young people with speech, language and communication needs. She works closely with students, families and staff to build confidence, strengthen communication and help every young person develop the skills they need to participate fully in learning and everyday life.
Josh Considine
Josh has over 10 years’ experience supporting young people with Special Educational Needs. He is passionate about the value of creativity and its positive impact on mental health and emotional wellbeing, using music to help people express emotions, improve communication, build confidence, reduce anxiety, and strengthen social connections.
Makiko
Makiko provides a safe and creative space where students can explore thoughts and emotions through art. Her therapeutic approach helps young people develop self-awareness, confidence and emotional resilience while encouraging positive strategies for managing wellbeing and building healthy relationships.

Lou is an experienced Feldenkrais Practitioner, movement specialist and qualified psychotherapist. Through movement, sensory integration and body-based approaches, she helps students improve coordination, emotional regulation and confidence, enabling them to engage more positively in learning and everyday life.
Luxmi
Therapies & Literacy Assistant
Luxmi supports students to develop their communication, language and literacy skills through individual and small-group sessions. Working alongside the wider therapy team, she helps students build confidence, practise new skills and apply them successfully within the classroom and throughout school life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Approach | Choice Theory & SEN Education
pageCache.text:
Our Approach
Helping each student build confidence, responsibility and a sense of belonging.
Every aspect of life at The Write Time is shaped by William Glasser’s Choice Theory, creating an environment where students feel safe, valued and empowered to succeed.
What Is Choice Theory?
At The Write Time, our approach is inspired by Dr. William Glasser’s Choice Theory, which recognises that all behaviour is driven by five basic human needs. By understanding these needs, we help students develop positive relationships, make responsible choices and become more engaged in their learning and personal development.
Every behaviour is driven by five basic human needs
Choice Theory Is How We Work
It’s how we work together every day.
From classroom learning to mentoring conversations, every interaction is guided by respect, positive relationships and helping students recognise the choices they have to shape their own future.
Choice Theory in Practice
When students feel safe, connected and understood, they’re more likely to engage in learning, build positive relationships and develop the confidence to make successful choices, both in school and beyond.
Taking Responsibility
Students learn to recognise the choices they make and understand how those choices influence their learning, relationships and future.
Understanding Behaviour
We see behaviour as communication. Rather than asking “What’s wrong with this student?” we ask “What need is this behaviour trying to meet?”
Building Positive Relationships
Strong relationships sit at the heart of everything we do. Staff encourage caring habits, respectful communication and mutual trust.
Developing a Positive Future
Every student is supported to build confidence, resilience and a personal vision for success, whatever that looks like for them.
What You’ll See Every Day
Developing Personal and Social Skills
Developing personal and social skills is just as important as academic progress. Through mentoring, coaching and everyday experiences, students build confidence, resilience and the practical skills they need to succeed both in school and beyond.
The Write Time School employs full-time Outreach Development Tutors (ODTs) to support students’ positive behaviour and personal growth. Each student is assigned an ODT and follows a Personal Development Plan, setting goals based on 8 key skills, including Positive behaviour, time management, critical thinking, effort, teamwork, leadership, negotiation and communication.
“The Write Time provides students with the opportunity to improve their life chances and have a positive future.”
Our aim is simple
To create a school where every young person feels they belong, believes in their own potential and leaves with the confidence, qualifications and life skills to succeed beyond The Write Time.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding Policy | The Write Time School
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
We are committed to creating an open, honest and respectful school community for everyone.
What is Safeguarding?
Safeguarding is the action we take to promote the welfare of children and protect them from harm. It’s everyone’s responsibility.
Got a concern?
Contact our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL): Emma Dear (DSL) emmadear@thewritetime.org.uk | 07852 989992Or Debbie Brindle-Carter (DDSL) debbiebrindle-carter@thewritetime.org.uk | 07903 351 472Or Lana Philippson (DDSL) lanaphilippson@thewritetime.org.uk | 07572 710635
Or get in touch with:
• Croydon SPOC – 020 8255 2888• Lewisham MASH – 020 8314 6660• Bromley MASH – 020 8461 7373 / 7379 / 7026• Bexley MASH – 020 3045 5440• Sutton SPOC – 020 8770 6001• Merton MASH – 020 8545 4226 / 4227• Wandsworth MASH – 020 8871 6000
Find help
The Write Time is committed to facilitating an environment where everyone feels confident about reporting any incidents of child-on-child abuse or sexual harassment and knowing that they will be heard and supported. We follow the guidance in the Department for Education’s Keeping Children Safe in education guidance at all times – as outlined in our safeguarding policy.
The NSPCC has a dedicated helpline for children and young people who have experienced abuse at school, or for worried adults and professionals that need support and guidance, including for non-recent abuse. t: 0800 136 663.
If you’re worried about your boyfriend or partner’s behaviour, learning more about the warning signs of domestic violence could help you – or someone close to you – stay safe. Refuge offers advice about domestic abuse for teenage girls and young people. t: 0808 2000 247
The Hide Out also offers advice for children and young people about domestic abuse.
If you are worried about a young person who might be in an abusive relationship, you can find out more information about teenage abusive relationships and how to get help. You can also call Childline to talk about any concerns you might have. They have trained counsellors there to support you. t: 0800 1111
The Write Time believe that everyone in the school community has the right to learn and to teach in a supportive and caring environment without fear of being bullied. We will help all members of the school community to benefit from computing and online technologies, whilst understanding its risks, and equip children with the knowledge and skills to be able to use it safely and responsibly.
If you would like advice about how to stay safe online visit thinkyouknow.co.uk They also have information about online blackmailing and how to access help if you need it.
Common Sense Media has useful reviews and advice by parents and children of all the latest games, apps and films.
The Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre (CEOP) offers advice on online safety. If you have been a victim of sexual online abuse or you’re worried this is happening to someone you know, you can let CEOP know safely and securely on their website.
Please encourage your child to speak to any member of our staff if they have any worries about bullying.
All The Write Time staff are committed to doing everything they can to prevent all kinds of bullying.
We want our school to be an environment which is safe, supportive and free from intimidation. We actively promote a culture of awareness, tolerance and inclusion where all forms of bullying are seen as unacceptable. You can find more details in our our anti-bullying policy.
Bullying UK offers lots of advice for young people and parents about bullying. You can also call their helpline t: 0808 800 2222.
Childline is there to help anyone under 19 in the UK with any issue they’re going through. You can talk about anything. Whether it’s something big or small, their trained counsellors are there to support you. t: 0800 1111
We understand the importance of providing support and resources for students who may be struggling with mental health issues, and we have a range of measures in place to ensure that they receive the help they need. Our goal is to create a safe and supportive environment where all students can thrive, and we are committed to working with our students, parents, and staff to achieve this.
Please speak to our SENCO (Lana Philippson) if you have any worries about mental health.
Mind is a mental health charity which provides support to everyone who has experienced a mental health problem. If you are concerned about your own mental health or about someone you know, you can contact Mind for advice t: 0300 1233393 or text 86463.
YoungMinds offers information and advice about children and young people’s wellbeing and mental health. They have lots of advice for young people about coping with mental health issues. They also have a helpline for parents and carers t: 0808 8025544.The Kooth team provide free, safe and anonymous online support and counselling for young people.
Samaritans are available, day or night, for anyone who’s struggling to cope, who needs someone to listen without judgement or pressure. They give people ways to cope and the skills to be there for others. And they encourage, promote and celebrate those moments of connection between people that can save lives. They offer listening and support to people and communities in times of need. You can call free on 116 123.
If you’re worried that a child or young person might be or is at risk of being exploited by a county lines gang, you must share your concerns. Please speak to our school’s designated safeguarding lead (Lana Philippson) or a member of staff.If you think a child is in immediate danger, contact the police on 999.
The NSPCC have lots of information and expert advice about how to support a young person who may be at risk of gang involvement or involved in county lines. t: 0808 800 5000 e: help@nspcc.org.uk
You can also contact Crimestoppers (anonymously) on 0800 555 111
A useful government guide for parents and carers has lots of advice about keeping children and young people safe and how to get support if you need it.
The guide includes information about:
Protecting children from domestic abuse
Teenage relationship abuse
Child sexual abuse and exploitation
Sexual assault referral centres
Protecting children from radicalisation
Online child safety
Mental health
